why: Permutations with a used array and duplicate digits: sort the digits and, at each position, skip a digit equal to the previous one that is not in use, so [0,0,1,2] gives each time once; then keep only valid HH:MM.
hints: Four digits have at most 24 orderings. How do equal digits create the same time twice, and how can you avoid generating it at all?
Sort the digits. At each slot, try every unused digit, but skip digit i when it equals digit i - 1 and digit i - 1 is unused: that branch was already explored.
When four digits are placed, check hour <= 23 and minute <= 59 and format with two digits each. Because the digits are sorted, valid times come out in chronological order.
pitfalls: Leading zeroes must be kept: 01:02, not 1:2.
Hours 24..29 are invalid even though the first digit is 2.
A set of strings also removes duplicates, but then you must sort.
